thought.text: Backend is confirmed running (`Tomcat started on port 8080`, `Started UrboCmsApplicationKt`). The leftover cms serve is on drifted port 34903. Let me clean up and start cms (39002) + app (39001) sequentially — builds are now fully cached:

reasoning_content:
The backend is confirmed to be running: `Tomcat started on port 8080`, `Started UrboCmsApplicationKt in 147.556 seconds` ✓.

Also, I can see that the cms serve process (161930) is running — according to its logs, it's serving on port **34903** (yet another port drift! The cms serve that got killed... no wait, actually, this is a cms serve that re-allocated 34903). And the boards log shows 39003 ✓.

So the current state: boards on 39003 (matches nginx), the leftover cms serve on 34903 (nginx expects 39002 → 502), and app is stopped.

Given the persistent memory pressure, the most robust final approach for getting all three running simultaneously is: **stop the leftover cms serve, then restart app and cms with NODE_OPTIONS heap limits, one at a time, each waiting for the other to finish building**.

No, wait. Let me think about what's actually consuming memory right now: boards (running) + containers + leftover cms serve (34903, already built = steady state). If the cms serve process is already built and in steady state, then its memory should be moderate. Let me check what's running and how much memory is available, then decide:

Option A: Kill the leftover cms serve; start cms (port 39002, cached build) and app (port 39001, cached build) sequentially. If both can fit in steady state, all three will be up simultaneously.

Key insight from the earlier measurement: steady state (after build) = app ~1.8GB + boards ~1.1GB... actually, the steady state after build is much lighter than during the build. The OOM always happens during the build phase of the 3rd server. Since the builds are now fully cached (nx daemon + esbuild cache), the build phase is short and light.

Let me try: kill the leftover cms serve, then start cms (39002) and app (39001) sequentially.

action.command:
# Kill the leftover drifted cms serve
kill -TERM -- -161929 2>/dev/null; sleep 6
ps aux | grep -E "run-executor|nx.js" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -r kill 2>/dev/null; sleep 4
cd /workspace
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
setsid nohup bash -c 'exec just serve --apps=cms < /dev/zero' > /tmp/zz-cms.log 2>&1 &
echo "cms pid $!"
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39002/ 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "cms UP check $i"; break; }
  echo "check $i: cms=$code avail=$(free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print $6}')MB"
  sleep 40
done
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "cms direct: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:39002/ 2>/dev/null
